messages:
Eve: uploaded a perfetto trace — weird fanout where client span IDs seem duplicated across runtime workers, KV-cache heatmap shows a dense hotspot right before a series of kernel switches. link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcdef :eyes:
Marcos: :eyes: can you share the raw trace pb + the nsys capture? did this start after the batching heuristic tweak last deploy?
Eve: trace pb uploaded to s3://redwood-traces/1994501122/trace.pb, nsys tar at s3://redwood-traces/1994501122/nsys.tar.gz. It correlates with last deploy around 1994500000. Short repro: heavy client->gateway p95 requests spike then tails.
Jun: quick thought — sounds like requests are getting split across kernels after kv cache misses, causing duplicate upstream spans as the runtime retries/pin-handoff. I saw a similar nvprof pattern where `kernel_select` flips mid-request. grep for `kv_cache_lookup` gaps in the trace.
perfetto-bot: auto-annotate: detected 47 kernel_swaps between 00:01:12 and 00:01:18, 12 flow discontinuities with matching client_req_id. (summary attached)
Nina: suggested triage: 1) run perfetto with flow events to correlate client->gateway->runtime request_id, 2) capture kernel names as counters, 3) generate kv-heatmap from trace. Example command:
```bash
perfetto --config perfetto_cfg.pbtxt -o trace.pb
python tools/trace_heatmap.py trace.pb --span "client_request" --kernels
```
Eve: also try this quick perfetto UI filter to isolate the region: 
```js
// in perfetto UI console
trace_tracks.filter(t => t.name.includes('kvcache') || t.name.includes('kernel_select') || t.name.includes('client_span'))
```
Marcos: good call. Also consider tagging requests at gateway with `routing_tag=<bin>` so trace flow shows which runtime pool handled the request — avoids false-duplicates from log-level merges. For repro, run 100 concurrent short requests with wrk2: `wrk2 -t8 -c100 -d60s --latency --timeout 10s http://gateway/req`
Jun: I'll pull the nsys capture now and run a hotspot summary + kernel timeline overlay, should have results in a few hours. If kernel_select is the hot path, we can try reverting the heuristic change in a canary and compare golden traces.
Eve: pasted quick nsys summary snippet from the tar:
```
Kernel: kernel_select    42.1%
KV Lookup: kv_cache_lookup 18.3%
Memcpy: memcopy_htod      11.7%
Other:                 27.9%
```
Nina: :thumbsup: if Jun confirms kernel_select regressions, plan: (A) create an urgent perf job that runs golden vs current for 5k requests, (B) add a trace flag at gateway for routing_tag, (C) revert batching heuristic in canary. I'll make a ticket.
Marcos: linking to infra ticket for canary rollout: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGRT-2942
Eve: thanks all — leaving trace notes in the S3 folder and will add a small repro harness. Ping me if you need SSH to the repro runner. :rocket:
